answer: Scarce-work identity ledger: each identity must carry a signed log of unique, externally verified labor hours (e.g., labeled data only it produced). A new member attaches under an existing vine of work records, and every identity needs a lantern review by two unrelated reviewers before its first transaction clears. Duplicate or copied logs trip a reef check that flags identical provenance hashes. Cost to an attacker: real verified hours plus reviewer attention per identity, so mass registration means mass labor, not mass payment.
